findings.title: Processing failures are marked complete and committed
findings.body: This runs in `finally`, so an exception from `result_processor` still removes the offset from the outstanding set. The commit loop can then advance past a result that was never processed; failures swallowed by `ResultProcessor.__call__` have the same outcome. Do not mark an offset complete until processing succeeds or the message is explicitly routed to a failure-handling path.

findings.title: Closing a strategy permanently shuts down the shared queue pool
findings.body: `queue_pool` is owned by `ResultsStrategyFactory` and reused by each `create_with_partitions` call, but closing one strategy shuts it down. When Arroyo recreates a strategy after a partition-assignment change, the factory reuses this non-None pool with stopped workers and shut-down queues. Subsequent submissions fail, and `submit()` treats those failures as completed offsets, allowing results to be committed without processing. Keep the shared pool alive across strategy instances, or create and manage a separate pool per strategy.

findings.title: A missing Kafka offset can permanently block commits
findings.body: The tracker requires every integer offset between `start` and `max_offset` to have been received. Kafka consumers can legitimately observe gaps, for example when compacted or aborted records are not returned. The first such gap makes this loop stop advancing even when every delivered message is complete; later messages then remain uncommitted and may be replayed indefinitely. Track the order of observed messages rather than requiring numeric adjacency.

findings.title: The queues are unbounded and provide no backpressure
findings.body: `queue.Queue()` defaults to an unlimited size, and `submit()` can keep adding work without waiting for workers. If Kafka intake outpaces processing, queued `WorkItem`s and their message payloads can grow without limit until the consumer runs out of memory. Use bounded queues and propagate saturation back to polling or another explicit backpressure mechanism.

findings.title: Queue shutdown APIs are unavailable before Python 3.13
findings.body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On supported Python runtimes before 3.13, this call raises `AttributeError` and is swallowed; workers remain blocked in `get()`, and `shutdown()` then waits up to five seconds per worker before leaving daemon threads behind. Use a shutdown mechanism compatible with the project's minimum Python version or require Python 3.13+.

findings.title: A negative worker count creates a pool that commits without processing
findings.body: `max_workers` is accepted as an unrestricted integer, and a negative value is truthy, so it produces a negative `num_queues` and starts no workers. Submissions then index an empty queue list; the strategy catches that error and marks the message offset complete, so results can be committed without processing. Reject non-positive worker counts before creating the pool.
